19.text: The shamanistic call manifests itself in various ways. Sometimes it is

20.text: an inner voice, which bids the person enter into intercourse with the “spirits.”

21.text: If the person is dilatory in obeying, the calling “spirit” soon appears in some

22.text: outward, visible shape, and communicates the call in a more explicit way.

23.text: For instance, Aiñanwaˊt, whom I have mentioned before, says that at one

24.text: time, after a severe illness, when his soul was ripe for inspiration, he saw

25.text: several “spirits,” but did not give much heed to the fulfilment of their orders.

26.text: Then a “spirit” came to him. He was gaunt, and black of color, and said

27.text: that he was the “spirit” of reindeer-scab.⁴ Aiñanwaˊt felt himself very much

28.text: drawn toward that “spirit,” and wanted him to stay and become his constant

29.text: companion. The “spirit” hesitated at first, and then refused to stay. He

30.text: said, however, “I may consent, if your desire for my company is strong

31.text: enough, — if you wish me enough to take the drum, to handle it for three
